title: Concern verification and diagnostic strategy
learningObjective: Translate customer concern into testable symptoms and initial plan

equipment.label: Work-order input (developmental stand-in)
equipment.notes: Minimal original stand-in authored for this lab. It provides a written customer concern only. It is not a completed service-write-up tool, has no persistence, and does not produce a repair order.

equipment.label: Service information lookup
equipment.notes: Not available. No approved service-information source exists in this repository and the source-rights status of the uploaded references is unverified. This lab therefore requires students to state which information they would need and where it must come from, instead of presenting a lookup interface.

points: Verify the concern before planning work; an unverified concern cannot be diagnosed.
Record the exact conditions under which the concern occurs, including when it does not occur.
State any assumption you make, and state what evidence would confirm or refute it.
Do not begin a repair plan from a customer description alone.
safetyBriefing.boundaries: Simulated and paper-based only. No vehicle is inspected, no test is performed, and no manufacturer procedure or specification is provided or implied.

instructorDemonstration.summary: Demonstrate converting an ambiguous customer statement into a verifiable symptom statement, then into an ordered test plan with stated assumptions.
steps: Read the supplied customer concern and identify the vague terms in it.
Rewrite the concern as a symptom statement that states conditions and a measurable observation.
List two competing causes that the symptom alone cannot separate.
State the first test and what result would change the plan.
Show what happens when service information is unavailable: state the need rather than guessing a specification.

scenario.symptom: Supplied customer concern: 'It runs rough sometimes and the light comes on, mostly when I am getting on the highway.' No measurement has been supplied yet.
scenario.systemContext: Concern verification and strategy only. Students must turn an ambiguous statement into a testable symptom, name the missing information, and justify an ordered plan without performing a diagnosis.

measurements.label: Supplied customer concern (written statement, not a measurement)
measurements.value: rough running sometimes; warning lamp illuminated; reported mainly under highway acceleration
measurements.conditions: customer-reported conditions only; not observed or verified
measurements.limitations: A customer statement is not a measurement. It is unverified, subjective and incomplete, and it must not be treated as a confirmed symptom.

descriptors: No waveform is supplied in Week 2. No scope work is expected.
Students state whether a scope observation would even be an appropriate first step, and why or why not.
waveformEvidence.notes: No sampled trace is supplied and none is implied.

scenario.uncertainty: The concern is unverified and the vehicle is unidentified. Students must state what is unknown and what must be established before any measurement plan is meaningful.

competingHypotheses.statement: The reported concern reflects a real intermittent condition that only occurs under the stated highway-acceleration conditions.
evidenceFor: The customer states a repeatable condition and a consistent operating context.
evidenceAgainst: The report is subjective, unverified, and no measurement or stored data has been supplied to support it.

competingHypotheses.statement: The reported concern is a misdescription of normal behaviour, or a condition unrelated to the system the customer suspects.
evidenceFor: Vague terms such as 'runs rough' and 'sometimes' can describe several unrelated conditions.
evidenceAgainst: A warning lamp was reported, which suggests a monitored condition was detected by the control system.

testSelectionOptions.label: Verify the concern by stating conditions and a measurable observation before any test
testSelectionOptions.justificationPrompt: Explain why concern verification must precede test selection, and what makes a symptom statement testable.
testSelectionOptions.expectedObservation: A rewritten symptom statement that names conditions, frequency and an observable effect.

testSelectionOptions.label: Identify the missing vehicle and system information before planning
testSelectionOptions.justificationPrompt: Explain which vehicle and system details are required before any plan is meaningful, and why guessing them is unacceptable.
testSelectionOptions.expectedObservation: A stated list of unknown items that must be established, with the reason each matters.

testSelectionOptions.label: Draft an ordered plan with explicit assumptions and decision points
testSelectionOptions.justificationPrompt: Explain how each planned step would change your thinking if the result differed from expectation.
testSelectionOptions.expectedObservation: An ordered plan in which every step states what result would confirm or refute a competing hypothesis.

prompts: Rewrite the supplied customer concern as a testable symptom statement.
List everything about the vehicle and system that remains unknown, and why each item matters.
State which information source you would need, and why an unverified source cannot be used as authority.
Describe your first planned test and the result that would change your plan.

steps: Restate the original concern and confirm the symptom statement still describes it.
Confirm each plan step names the observation that would confirm or refute it.
expectedEvidence: A symptom statement an instructor could verify or refute from the same information.
A plan in which no step depends on an unstated assumption.

accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab from the skip link to the work-order panel, then through the hypothesis cards, test-selection buttons and worksheet fields using standard form navigation.
textAlternatives: The customer concern is presented as text and is also read by the work-order stand-in panel.
All hypothesis and test information is text; no information is conveyed by colour or position alone.
notes: No instrument is mounted in this lab, so no canvas or animated element is present.
Status and selection feedback is announced through a polite live region.
Worksheet fields are labelled and reachable in document order.

technicalReviewChecklist.statement: Customer concern is clearly labelled unverified and is not presented as a measurement.
No manufacturer procedure, specification or service-information content is presented.
The missing service-information asset is disclosed in the lab, not simulated.
Work-order stand-in is described as a limited developmental input, not a completed tool.
Instructor material is stored outside the student tree and is not reachable from this page.
